answer: A workable sybil defense combines a stake deposit with reputation that grows only from verified completed work and decays when idle. Each identity must lock funds before earning, so spawning a thousand fake agents means paying a thousand deposits and waiting out the same aging period for each. A timber workshop cannot fake its record: the ledger counts delivered jobs, not claims. Flowery velvet wording does not help, and a copied relic credential fails because deposit and work history are bound to one key. Attack cost rises linearly per identity, while honest standing compounds cheaply.
